name: ZIMBABWE

flag.title: Flag of Zimbabwe
flag.note: Seven stripes; Zimbabwe Bird on triangle

lead: Zimbabwe sits landlocked in southern Africa, where 900-year-old stone ruins gave the country its name. Victoria Falls — heard 40 km away — and Lake Kariba, the world's biggest man-made lake, live here. Elephant-packed savannah, ancient granite fortresses, and more official languages than any nation: Africa's wonder-packed heartland.
geo: Zimbabwe sits on a high central plateau — the Highveld — at around 1,200 m, so it stays cooler than you'd expect near the equator. The Zambezi borders the north, then plunges over Victoria Falls: 1.7 km wide, 108 m tall, with spray that forms a permanent rainbow.

The Eastern Highlands rise to Mount Nyangani at 2,592 m — cold enough for frost in winter. Lake Kariba, formed when a dam was completed in 1959, stretches 280 km along the Zambian border and powers millions of homes.
animals: Zimbabwe is Big Five country — lion, leopard, rhino, elephant, and buffalo all roam here. Hwange National Park shelters around 40,000 elephants, one of Earth's densest populations, plus giraffe, zebra, and wild dogs.

The African painted dog is one of Zimbabwe's most endangered animals — about 660 in 86 packs, each with a unique coat like a fingerprint. The Zambezi also hosts enormous Nile crocodiles and huge pods of hippos.
culture: The Shona people — about 70% of Zimbabwe — have played the mbira, a thumb piano with metal keys, for over 1,000 years. It summons ancestors during healing ceremonies called bira, and its layered sound has influenced musicians worldwide.

The daily staple is sadza — stiff maize porridge scooped by hand and dipped into meat or pumpkin-leaf stew. The Ndebele people are famed for bold geometric murals painted on home walls in black, white, and red.
history: About 900 years ago the Shona kingdom built a hilltop city of stacked granite — no mortar, just skill. It housed 18,000 people and traded gold as far as China. 'Zimbabwe' means 'great stone houses' in Shona.

British colonists arrived in 1890, renaming the land Rhodesia. On 18 April 1980 Zimbabwe raised its flag — the last African country to win independence from Britain. A new era opened in 2017 when Emmerson Mnangagwa took power.
wows: Zimbabwe has 16 official languages — a Guinness World Record for the most of any country.
In 2009 Zimbabwe printed a 100 trillion dollar note — the largest denomination ever — worth ~40 US cents.
Victoria Falls is so loud its roar carries 40 km, earning its Shona name: The Smoke That Thunders.
Lake Kariba is the world's largest man-made reservoir by volume — about 180 cubic kilometres of water.
Zimbabwe has more ancient rock-art sites than anywhere else in southern Africa, painted over 13,000 years.
Each African painted dog has a unique coat; no two wild dogs in the world look exactly the same.
Great Zimbabwe ruins cover 80 hectares — the biggest pre-modern stone complex in sub-Saharan Africa.

myths.myth: Zimbabwe is just one big hot desert
myths.fact: Its central Highveld plateau sits at 1,200 m, keeping temperatures mild. The Eastern Highlands get heavy rain and frost on the peaks in winter.

myths.myth: Victoria Falls is mostly on the Zambia side
myths.fact: Zimbabwe faces 75% of the falls. The widest, most dramatic sections — Main Falls and Rainbow Falls — are best seen from the Zimbabwean bank.
